llm.summary: The skill discloses its Crawlora dependency, but its helper can call broader Crawlora endpoints and can send the API key to an overridden API base.

dimensions.detail: The helper reads CRAWLORA_API_BASE from the environment without validation and attaches the API key to requests, so a misconfigured or influenced environment could redirect the credential.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hook, package dependency, background service, or automatic execution was found; setup only asks the user to provide CRAWLORA_API_KEY.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and reference/endpoints.md scope use to /apple-jobs/search and /apple-jobs/job, while the helper comments and implementation support unrelated Amazon, YouTube, Google, and trends requests.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill uses a Crawlora API key but does not show local privilege escalation, persistent system changes, memory writes, or access to unrelated local secrets.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is Apple job research through two Apple Jobs endpoints, but scripts/crawlora.sh is a generic Crawlora client with arbitrary path, method, and body support.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable using Crawlora as a third-party API provider. Keep the API key low-privilege if possible, avoid sensitive search terms, do not set CRAWLORA_API_BASE unless you fully trust the destination, and prefer a version that restricts the helper to /apple-jobs/search and /apple-jobs/job.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in context: the helper's documented examples cover non-Apple Crawlora endpoints, which is broader than the skill's Apple-jobs-only purpose.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in context: the script accepts any path and appends it to the Crawlora base URL instead of enforcing the two documented Apple Jobs endpoints.
[SQP-2] expected: Downgraded in context: third-party transmission to Crawlora is disclosed in SKILL.md, but the generic POST/body support remains broader than the Apple Jobs workflow.
[E1] expected: Partly expected: sending Apple job search terms and job IDs to Crawlora is central and disclosed, but arbitrary paths and POST bodies exceed the documented scope.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted in context: CRAWLORA_API_BASE is caller-controlled and unvalidated while the x-api-key header is always attached.
